title: Matched population but different endpoint and follow-up

patient_context.chief_complaint: The two studies now enrolled the same broad population. Does 62% versus 48% establish A is better?
patient_context.history: Controlled change: both trials use the same target population, but Trial A still uses endpoint EA at week 12 and Trial B endpoint EB at week 24.

interaction.prompt: Update the comparability assessment after population matching while preserving the remaining endpoint/follow-up differences.

must_include: Acknowledge that matching the population removes one comparability problem.
State that different endpoint definitions and follow-up times still prevent a clean direct superiority claim.
Demonstrate partial belief updating rather than repeating every original objection unchanged.
must_not_claim: Do not say all comparability problems are solved.
Do not ignore the controlled change that populations are now matched.
acceptable_actions: Return DIRECT_SUPERIORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED with fewer remaining objections.
expected_behavior.uncertainty_behavior: Confidence in noncomparability should be tied to the remaining design differences.

forbidden_claims: matched population alone makes the percentages directly comparable

critical_errors: Fails to update after the population variable changes.
Declares superiority while ignoring remaining endpoint/time differences.
